question:
A 49-year-old male patient presents with complaints of fatigue and blurry vision for the past month,
along with an unintentional weight loss of 4.5 kg (10 lb) over six months. His oxygen saturation is 99%
on room air. Laboratory findings reveal a hemoglobin of 17.5 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume of 88
μm3, increased red cell volume, and elevated serum erythropoietin concentration. What is the most
likely cause of these clinical and laboratory findings? Answer Choices: (A) Polycythemia vera (B) Renal
cell carcinoma (C) Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (D) Von Hippel-Lindau disease (E)
Cerebellar hemangioblastoma (F) Primary pulmonary hypertension (G) Chronic myelogenous leukemia
(H) Pheochromocytoma (I) Hepatocellular carcinoma (J) Sleep apnea syndrome
 A. Primary pulmonary hypertension
B. Renal cell carcinoma
C. Von Hippel-Lindau disease
D. Polycythemia vera
E. Chronic myelogenous leukemia
F. Hepatocellular carcinoma
G. Sleep apnea syndrome
H. Cerebellar hemangioblastoma
I. Pheochromocytoma
J. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
